sources.title: CRAFT: Coaching Reinforcement Learning Autonomously using Foundation Models for Multi-Robot Coordination Tasks
DeepFleet: Multi-Agent Foundation Models for Mobile Robots

questions: Can foundation models improve embodied swarms while preserving decentralized execution, scaling to many inexpensive agents, and degrading gracefully under communication, member, sensor, and model failures?

direction.question: Can foundation models improve embodied swarms while preserving decentralized execution, scaling to many inexpensive agents, and degrading gracefully under communication, member, sensor, and model failures?
direction.closureCriteria: Show increasing team utility across at least three swarm sizes; keep execution decentralized with explicit per-agent compute and bandwidth caps; compare against strong modular decentralized baselines; test packet loss, partitions, Byzantine or faulty members, sensor corruption, and model failure; and transfer to a physical swarm.
partialResults: CRAFT uses language and vision-language foundation models to coach reinforcement learning for multi-robot coordination, and DeepFleet trains multi-agent foundation models on warehouse fleet movement data. RoCo and SMART-LLM coordinate smaller robot teams with language models. These invalidate a claim that the combination is nearly untouched, while leaving scalable online decentralized swarm intelligence and fault tolerance unresolved.
starters: Individual: In ARGoS or Crazyswarm2 simulation, compare a local foundation-model coach with a modular decentralized controller across swarm sizes and a fixed packet-loss, sensor-noise, and member-dropout matrix.
Small lab: Test six to twelve inexpensive robots under packet loss, partitions, robot dropout, and stale or adversarial guidance; include centralization and communication-budget ablations.

Well-funded lab: Run a 50-plus heterogeneous-robot, multi-site study of online shared learning with decentralized execution, predefined graceful-degradation curves, safety supervision, and independent robustness auditing.

noveltyReview.scope: Targeted arXiv searches for foundation models in multi-robot coordination, fleet foundation models, LLM robot collaboration, decentralized swarm learning, embodied swarms, communication failures, and 2025-2026 follow-on papers; reference chaining from CRAFT, DeepFleet, RoCo, and SMART-LLM.
noveltyReview.note: Medium confidence that scalable, online, decentralized and fault-tolerant foundation-model swarms remain open. CRAFT and DeepFleet already demonstrate large-model coordination in smaller robot teams, narrowing the unresolved target. No priority claim is made.

counterexamples: CRAFT trains coordinated multi-quadruped navigation and bimanual manipulation policies with foundation-model coaching and reports physical-policy transfer, but it is not a large, cheap, online-adaptive swarm under broad failures.

DeepFleet models warehouse fleets using data from hundreds of thousands of operational robots and robot-centric local graphs, but focuses on prediction and fleet design using proprietary operational data rather than general online swarm control.
RoCoBench and SMART-LLM show language-model planning for small multi-robot teams; scale, decentralization, latency, and graceful degradation remain limited.

literature.t: CRAFT: Coaching Reinforcement Learning Autonomously using Foundation Models for Multi-Robot Coordination Tasks
DeepFleet: Multi-Agent Foundation Models for Mobile Robots

benchmarks: Crazyswarm2 or ARGoS with a standardized communication-and-fault suite
datasets: RoCoBench language, plan, and trajectory tasks
A new open, fault-annotated multi-robot trajectory corpus; no canonical open foundation-model swarm corpus was identified

estimated.individual: One modern GPU plus 16-64 CPU cores for simulation.
estimated.smallLab: Four to twelve low-cost ground robots or three to six drones, four to eight GPUs, localization, spares, and safety supervision.
estimated.wellFundedLab: Thirty-two to one hundred robots, mixed embodiments, motion capture or UWB localization, wireless instrumentation, safety operators, and substantial model-training compute.

direction.crowdedness: Medium for language-model multi-robot planning; low-medium for decentralized foundation-model swarms with systematic fault tolerance.
direction.tractability: High in simulation, medium for a small physical fleet, and low for large heterogeneous swarms with convincing safety and robustness.
